ideas.title: Tensor normal form: the m=2 Weil-descended S_3 system is a Boolean bilinear system whose 3-tensor is the restricted multiplication tensor of V; d_F is a functional of that tensor, not of the curve or of n
ideas.statement: Verified in this pass (ffd_semaev_core.build_system, n=7,9,10, 9 instances): every descended equation has only monomials a_j*b_l, a_j, b_l, 1 (zero a_j*a_l or b_l*b_m or cubic terms). Equivalently the system is the K-equation a*b + Phi(a) + Phi(b) = kappa with a,b in V, Phi = z*G(sigma(.)) F_2-linear, i.e. n Boolean equations a^T M_i b + ell_i(a,b) = c_i where (M_i) are the coordinate bilinear forms of mu_V: V x V -> K, (a,b) -> ab/z. Hypothesis: the last fall degree d_F is determined by the 3-tensor T_V in F_2^{k x k x n} (plus the affine part), and the deviation of d_F (4-5) from the generic bilinear value (FSS: k+2 = ceil(n/2)+2, which coincides with the treatise's proved upper bound) is caused by T_V having tensor rank exactly n over K-bar (diagonalised by the n Frobenius embeddings) versus ~n^2/8 for a random k x k x n tensor.
ideas.mechanism: Replace the multiplication tensor by controlled surrogates while keeping the affine part and the Boolean field equations: (i) random dense tensor of shape (k,k,n); (ii) random F_2-tensor of rank exactly n (sum of n random rank-one lambda_r x mu_r x nu_r); (iii) random tensor of rank R for R in {n, 2n, 3n, 4n}; (iv) the true Semaev tensor for random V and for Semaev's polynomial subspace (convolution/Toeplitz tensor). Measure the Boolean refutation degree d_F (closure W_d, 1 in W_d) for unsatisfiable targets. If d_F is a function of tensor rank/structure only, open problem 12 becomes a statement about Boolean bilinear systems of bounded tensor rank, a clean random model where Hilbert functions and pseudo-solutions can be computed and (plausibly) proved; the curve enters only through kappa and Phi.
ideas.wall_bypassed: TREAT-first-fall-degree-constant (scope: no presentation has a proved last-fall lower bound growing with n) and KN-OPEN-8f3d27 / open problem 12. Also goes around TREAT-digit-presentation-growth's 'curve-free null' by making the null explicit (the tensor), rather than reproducing a law.
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: The wall is a statement about the absence of a proof technique. The bilinear/tensor reformulation is not in any programme file (grep for bilinear, tensor rank, Moore, Hadamard, bihomogeneous over brief/*, treatise/*.tex, MAP_ideas_corpus.json, LEAD_ATLAS: zero hits except an unrelated 'bilinear map' in a Cheon card). The programme's own upper bound k+2 (fix c=a+b, affine in a) is exactly the FSS bilinear bound min(n_x,n_y)+2, which suggests the bilinear theory is the right ambient theory and that the observed 4-5 is a LOW-RANK effect, a quantity never varied in the programme (all experiments vary V, n, basis, target; none varies the tensor independently of the field).
ideas.nongenericity_argument: Theory item. It changes no cost by itself. It bears on B*D^2 << N only through lever 1: a proved d_F lower bound growing with the base dimension k (via the rank-n model) kills Semaev-type subexponential claims for these presentations; a proved f(m)-type bound would revive them. The experiment is designed to discriminate, not to attack.

Four arms at n in {11,13,15,17}, k=ceil(n/2), 6 unsatisfiable targets each: (A) Semaev descent on random V (ffd_semaev_core.build_system, exhaustively checked unsat); (B) same affine part (ell_i, c_i) with the bilinear part replaced by a random dense tensor of shape (k,k,n); (C) same with a random F_2-tensor of rank exactly n (n random rank-one terms, lambda_r, mu_r in F_2^k, nu_r in F_2^n); (D) rank R in {2n,3n}. Record d_F per instance (closure degree capped at 6; record '>=7' otherwise) and the Hilbert-type profile dim W_d cap B_{<=e}.

falsifier.tools: python3 + numpy; /Volumes/SSD990-2/crypto-autoresearcher/research/verification/ffd_semaev_core.py for arm A; msolve -g 2 over char 2 as a cross-check of refutation on 8 instances.
falsifier.prediction_if_true: Arm A and arm C agree (d_F in {3,4,5} on the same n-profile, within one degree on >= 80% of matched instances); arm B jumps to the bilinear generic regime (d_F >= 6 already at n=13, i.e. tracks k+2 or the Boolean semi-regular degree); arm D interpolates monotonically with R. Then d_F is a tensor-rank functional and the lower-bound problem is reduced to the rank-n random model.
falsifier.prediction_if_false: Arm C behaves like arm B (d_F >= 6 at n=13-17) while arm A stays at 3-5: then the Galois (Frobenius-conjugate) structure of the Semaev tensor, not its rank, carries the low degree, and idea MP-comm_alg-3 (single-generator K-closure) is the correct reduction instead; or arm B also stays at 3-5, in which case the affine part / Boolean constraints dominate and the tensor is irrelevant (then d_F growth cannot be read from the quadratic part at all).

ideas.risk: Degree cap 6 may be hit by arm B at n=17 (then record as a censored lower bound). Rank-exactly-n F_2 tensors are not the same as rank-n-over-K-bar tensors with F_2-descended structure; a negative on arm C does not refute the rank mechanism, only the F_2-rank surrogate (that is why arm D and idea 3 exist).

ideas.title: Split-algebra normal form of the top-form ideal: over K-bar the quadratic top forms of the descended S_3 are the n diagonal products sigma^i(a)*sigma^i(b) of Frobenius-conjugate linear forms; their Koszul homology, Hilbert function and zero set at infinity are explicit and V-independent
ideas.statement: Let y_i(a) = sum_j a_j v_j^{2^i} (i=0..n-1) be the n K-linear forms in the k variables a (a Moore matrix, rank k). Because K (x) K-bar = prod of n copies of K-bar via the embeddings sigma^i, the K-span of the n top bilinear forms Tr(delta_i ab) equals the span of the n products y_i(a) y_i(b). Consequences to test and then prove: (1) the top-form ideal I^top = (y_i(a)y_i(b))_i has >= 2n linear syzygies (sum_j v_j a_j * (ab)^top = sigma(a) b is degree 2 as a Boolean polynomial, a Frobenius collapse, giving a K-rank-1 linear syzygy per block), whereas n generic bilinear forms in P^{k-1} x P^{k-1} have none; (2) V(I^top) in P^{k-1} x P^{k-1} is a finite set of C(2k,k) points when n = 2k-1 (pairs of complementary coordinate supports S, S^c with k-1 <= |S| <= k in the Moore embedding), while n = 2k-1 generic bilinear forms have no common zero; (3) the Hilbert function of R/(I^top + (a_j^2, b_l^2)) depends only on (n,k) for generic V, hence so does Salizzoni's rigorous upper bound d_F <= d_reg(F^top)+1; (4) the Betti table of I^top is close to linear (Burity-Tohaneanu fold-product linear-resolution conjecture family), the structural reason the system is not semi-regular.
ideas.mechanism: Base change to K-bar diagonalises the multiplication tensor; all homological invariants (Hilbert function, Betti numbers, regularity) are invariant under field extension, so they can be computed over F_2 and interpreted over K-bar as a products-of-linear-forms ideal. Products of linear forms ideals have a combinatorial theory (fold products, star configurations, linear codes/generalised Hamming weights of the Moore code). This converts 'why is the descended system far from semi-regular' from a measurement into a computable, and plausibly provable, statement about an ideal generated by n products of pairs of linear forms in general position in two k-dimensional blocks.
ideas.wall_bypassed: KR-IC-58213c / KR-IC-0d2021 scope ('semi-regular predictions do not describe descended summation systems' with no replacement model) and the EXTERNAL_CORPUS gap 'Betti/syzygy tables of the Semaev ideal' (named untouched; MAP_ideas_corpus GAP entry).
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: Those closures assume the only available null is semi-regularity. The split-algebra form gives a second, structured null (diagonal products of linear forms) whose Hilbert function is computable without a Groebner basis and whose zero set at infinity (C(2k,k) bi-projective points) is explicit; the walls say nothing about ideals generated by products of linear forms.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: Theory/accounting item: no change in B or D by itself. Its value for the B*D^2 line is indirect: it supplies the rigorous upper bound d_F <= d_reg(F^top)+1 in closed form (if the Hilbert function has a closed form) and the candidate 'pseudo-solutions at infinity' (the C(2k,k) points) around which a lower-bound certificate for the affine system could be organised.

(2) Compute the Hilbert function of R/(I^top + squares) for degrees <= 2k for 5 random V and for the polynomial subspace at n=11,13; test V-independence (random V) and the polynomial-subspace deviation; read off d_reg(F^top) and compare with measured d_F from idea 1 arm A (Salizzoni: d_F <= d_reg+1 must hold on every instance; record tightness). (3) Count V(I^top) over F_{2^n}: enumerate projective points of P^{k-1}(F_{2^n}) x P^{k-1}(F_{2^n}) only for n=7,k=4 (15^2*... feasible: (2^28-1)/(2^7-1)=2113 points per factor, 4.5e6 pairs) and compare with C(8,4)=70 (plus points over extensions missed; expect exactly 70 K-rational points since the components are K-defined). (4) Compare the Hilbert function with the ideal of n random F_2-rational products ell_i(a) m_i(b) (general position) at the same (n,k).
falsifier.toy_params: n=7 (zero-set count), n=9,11,13 (syzygies, Hilbert function), k=ceil(n/2), degrees <= 2k; C(26,<=7) columns max ~ 1.3e6 -> restrict Hilbert function to degree <= 7 at n=13.
falsifier.tools: python3 + numpy (bit-packed GF(2) elimination); ffd_semaev_core.build_system for the forms; cypari2 for F_{2^n} arithmetic in the point count; msolve -g 1 (char 2, no field equations) as an independent leading-ideal/Hilbert check on two instances.
falsifier.prediction_if_true: Exactly 2n (random V) linear syzygies at degree 3 vs 0 for random bilinear forms; Hilbert function of R/(I^top+squares) identical across random V at fixed (n,k) and identical to the random-products-of-linear-forms ideal; 70 K-rational common zeros at n=7,k=4; d_reg(F^top)+1 >= measured d_F on all instances with gap <= 2.

ideas.risk: The C(2k,k) count assumes 'any k of the n Moore forms are independent' (generic V); degenerate V (e.g. V a subfield-like or Frobenius-stable space, impossible at prime n but possible at composite toy n) breaks it: use prime n only. Hilbert function over F_2 of the squares-added algebra at degree ~k is memory-heavy beyond n=13.

ideas.title: Single-generator K-closure: decompose the F_2 Boolean closure W_d(F) into the semilinear closure of ONE K-polynomial u = ab + Phi(a) + Phi(b) + kappa and 'cross-conjugate' falls; reduce open problem 12 to a one-generator problem over K
ideas.statement: The descended system F is the coefficient-wise trace of the single Boolean-variable polynomial u in B_K = K[a,b]/(a_j^2+a_j, b_l^2+b_l). Hence W_d(F) (x) K = the smallest sigma-stable degree-closed K-subspace containing u, which contains sum_i sigma^i(V^K_d(u)) where V^K_d(u) is the K-closure of u alone. Define d_K(u) = min{d : 1 in V^K_d(u)} (refutation by the single generator without using its Frobenius conjugates) and d_F as usual; then d_F <= d_K. Hypothesis: (a) the gap d_K - d_F is bounded by 1 (the only cross-conjugate contributions are the Frobenius syzygies of THM_SEMAEV_FALL1 Lemma 1, e.g. l_0 = Tr(w^2 + w)); (b) d_K is governed by the degree of the multilinear interpolants of 1/u-type functions and is provably >= c*k for a positive constant c. (a)+(b) would give the first proved growing lower bound; (a) alone reduces the problem to a one-generator closure over a large field, where K-linear algebra (Moore determinants, Frobenius-semilinear maps) replaces F_2 combinatorics.
ideas.mechanism: The closure recursion commutes with K-scalars and with sigma acting on coefficients; the F_2-rational points are what make sigma matter (a_j^2 = a_j). Computing V^K_d(u) needs one K-row per monomial multiple (n times fewer rows than the F_2 Macaulay/closure matrix of F) with Gaussian elimination over F_{2^n}; comparing dim_K V^K_d(u) * n with dim_F2 W_d(F) degree by degree isolates exactly the falls that need two different conjugates. A lower bound for the one-generator closure can be attempted via K-valued pseudo-expectations E: B_K,<=d -> K with E(m u) = 0 (deg m <= d-2) and E(1) = 1, a K-linear system with 2^{2k} unknowns at full degree but only C(2k,<=d) at degree d, whose solvability is a rank condition on a structured (Moore-type) matrix.
ideas.wall_bypassed: TREAT-first-fall-degree-constant / KN-OPEN-8f3d27 (no proved growing lower bound) and LEAD-ICB-frobenius-search-symmetry (closed: 'Frobenius is an equivariance between conjugate instances, not a per-instance symmetry'; equivariant elimination a constant).
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: The Frobenius closure concerns using sigma as a SEARCH symmetry for speed. Here sigma is used to factor the PROOF object: W_d(F) is the Galois-descent of a sum of conjugates of a one-generator closure, and the question 'does d_F grow' splits into 'does d_K grow' (a statement about a single K-polynomial in Boolean variables, where Moore-matrix nondegeneracy arguments are available) and 'are cross-conjugate falls bounded'. Neither sub-question is in the atlas; THM_SEMAEV_FALL1 proves the collapse lemma but explicitly stops before any growth law.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: Theory item: no B or D change. If (a) holds and d_K is proved to grow with k, the subexponential heuristics for binary Weil-descent presentations are closed by theorem (treatise open problem 12); if d_K is also flat, the one-generator model is a cheaper laboratory (n times smaller matrices) for the (4,4),(4,5),(4,6) cells.

Programme: ffd_frobenius_witness.py (mu = x_R^{-2} kills the degree-2 part), THM_SEMAEV_FALL1.

ideas.title: Multigraded block law for chained systems: d_F is set by the smallest variable blocks (the m factor-base blocks of size l), not by the n-sized auxiliary blocks; test by artificially restricting the chain intermediates
ideas.statement: The chained descended system (m summands, t-1 intermediates y) is multihomogeneous of multidegree <= (1,...,1) in the blocks (a^{(1)},...,a^{(m)}, y^{(1)},...,y^{(t-1)}) up to Frobenius-collapsed lower terms (the e_2^2 term of S_3 is linear after Boolean reduction; only x_1 x_2 y is genuinely trilinear). For bilinear systems the generic degree of regularity is min(n_x,n_y)+2 (FSS 2011), and the treatise's proved k+2 at m=2 is this bound. Conjecture: for the chained system the solving degree is controlled by the smallest block sizes, d_F <= f(l, m) with f linear in l and INDEPENDENT of the y-block size n, which explains the measured flatness in n at fixed (m,l) and the measured growth ceil(l/2)+4 (m=3), l+4 (m=4). Testable new consequence: shrinking the y-blocks (restricting intermediates to an l'-dimensional subspace, a legitimate but yield-losing presentation) must NOT lower d_F while l' >= l, and must lower it once l' < l.
ideas.mechanism: Multigraded Macaulay matrices: rows m*f with m of multidegree (d_1,...,d_m, e_1,...,e_{t-1}); the (1,...,1) top forms plus Boolean squares generate; by FSS-type arguments the Hilbert bi-series exhausts the smaller block first, so the degree at which the quotient vanishes is governed by the small blocks. A matching lower bound for the chained system could follow the FSS Hilbert biseries argument restricted to the sub-block (a^{(1)}, a^{(2)}) where the system is bilinear-plus-collapse (idea 1). The y-restriction experiment separates 'block size' from 'n' cleanly for the first time (the programme always had y-blocks of size exactly n).
ideas.wall_bypassed: TREAT-first-fall-degree-constant scope ('measured D at m=3 fits ceil(l/2)+4; m=4 fits l+4; cells (4,4),(4,5),(4,6) unmeasured') and LEAD-ICE-descent-closure-degree-at-scale (open_blocked: does closure degree stay at 4 as l and n grow) and LEAD-ICE-semaev-chain-cost-model (closed: charged cost is topology-blind; revisit clause: 'a solver whose DEGREE depends on topology').
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: The cost-model closure assumes degree is a black box; here the degree is modelled by the multigraded block structure, which IS topology-dependent (a chain vs a balanced merge tree has different block incidence), so it addresses precisely the revisit clause. The treatise lists multigraded regularity as 'a second model' (open problem 1) but never ran it; the block-restriction test is new.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: Theory/accounting. A proved n-independent block law f(l,m) with l ~ n/m is still growing in n for fixed m, so it does not revive subexponential claims unless f is sublinear in l; conversely a proved linear-in-l lower bound would, at Semaev's optimum l ~ sqrt(n ln n), give d_F = Theta(sqrt(n ln n)), exactly killing the o(sqrt(n ln n)) requirement of Semaev 2015. No B*D^2 change by itself.

ideas.title: Exact F_2-Nullstellensatz degree of the descended system via trace interpolants: 1 = Tr(G*u) on the cube with G a K_0-coefficient multilinear polynomial; a computable, presentation-level upper bound on d_F with a candidate closed form via Lucas/Frobenius degree arguments
ideas.statement: Because span_F2 F = {Tr(delta u) : delta in K_0} + F_2 l_0 and the Boolean closure is contained in the Boolean ideal, any static Nullstellensatz certificate over F_2 has the form 1 = reduce(sum_m m * Tr(gamma_m u)) = Tr(G u) as functions on {0,1}^{2k}, with G = sum_m gamma_m m, gamma_m in K (K_0 plus the l_0 direction). So the F_2-Nullstellensatz degree is d_NS = 2 + min{deg G : G multilinear with K-coefficients, Tr(G(x) u(x)) = 1 for all x in the cube}; for the single K-equation without trace (idea 3's d_K) it is 2 + deg of the multilinear interpolant of 1/u, a function-table quantity. Hypotheses: (i) d_F <= d_NS always (PC degree <= NS degree); (ii) on the programme's instances d_NS - d_F <= 1 up to n ~ 21; (iii) the minimal degree of a K_0-valued G with Tr(G u) = 1 is a Boolean-function-complexity invariant (the 'trace degree' of 1/u over the subspace V), computable by linear algebra on 2^{2k} function values, and amenable to Lucas-theorem/Frobenius-degree lower-bound arguments (Gorla-Trebiani style) because u is bilinear+affine with values in a field of characteristic 2.
ideas.mechanism: Static certificates are a linear system over F_2 in the unknown coefficients of G restricted to degree <= d: the matrix has 2^{2k} rows (cube points) and n*C(2k,<=d) columns; its solvability gives d_NS exactly. Unlike the dynamic closure, d_NS has a direct functional interpretation (degree of a trace-interpolant of 1/u), so lower bounds on d_NS can be attacked with Boolean-function degree tools (Lucas' theorem on binomials mod 2, as in Gorla-Trebiani's exact d_reg for the ESF Hamming model; 2-adic/Frobenius degree of 1/u as a map K^{2k} -> K). If d_NS tracks d_F, a proved growth law for d_NS is a proved growth law for solving cost of static (XL/Macaulay-at-fixed-degree) refutations, and a strong heuristic for F4.
ideas.wall_bypassed: TREAT-first-fall-degree-constant (no proved growing lower bound) and KN-OPEN-3c8f51 ('what produces the degree-4 Macaulay refutation of most unsatisfiable m=2 S_3 descents'): the NS formulation names the object (a degree-<=2 trace interpolant G of 1/u exists iff refutation at degree 4).
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: The treatise's certificates are dynamic (closure) lower bounds, and the open problem asks for pseudo-solutions of the closure. The NS degree is a different, simpler invariant for which exact computation by function-table linear algebra is possible and for which Boolean-function-degree lower bounds (Lucas, Frobenius) are a known proof technology; nothing in the atlas computes or bounds d_NS for descended systems ('pc_degree_demo' measures the dynamic PC degree D*).
ideas.nongenericity_argument: Theory/accounting. A proved lower bound on d_NS bounds only static (Macaulay-at-degree-d / XL) refutations, i.e. it prices the XL arms the programme already measures ('plain Macaulay refutation tracks the semi-regular degree'); if d_NS - d_F stays <= 1 empirically, it is also the best available proxy for a dynamic lower bound. No change to B or D; honest class: theory.
ideas.prior_art: Treatise falldegree.tex (Thm reform: span F = {Tr(delta w)} + l_0, d_ff=2, upper bound k+2, certified d_F>=5 at n=33-45); THM_SEMAEV_FALL1 Lemma 1 (Frobenius collapse); Caminata-Gorla 2023; Huang-Kosters-Yeo 2015 / HKYY; Kousidis-Wiemers 2019; Steiner 2310.03637 (degree-fall lower bounds); Salizzoni 2304.13485; Faugere-Safey El Din-Spaenlehauer 2011 (bihomogeneous (1,1) systems, d_reg <= min(n_x,n_y)+2); Gorla-Trebiani 2609.14052 (proved d_reg via Hilbert function counting). Beame-Impagliazzo-Krajicek-Pitassi-Pudlak (Nullstellensatz degree, designs); Buss-Pitassi; Razborov 1998 and Alekhnovich-Razborov 2001 (PC degree lower bounds, pseudo-expectations); Clegg-Edmonds-Impagliazzo 1996 (PC vs NS gap); Gorla-Trebiani 2609.14052 (Lucas-theorem Hilbert-function proof of an exact Boolean d_reg); programme: pc_degree_demo (dynamic D*), Prop. cert (dual certificates), prog_binary 'SAT/WDSat are enumerators' (brute-force PC refutation 3l+1).
ideas.novelty_status: novelty_unverified (not searched; 'Nullstellensatz degree of Weil-descended Semaev systems' and the trace-interpolant characterisation are not in the programme files read; the PC/NS literature is classical but its application here was not found).

falsifier.design: python3: for the m=2 descended S_3 instances of idea 1 arm A at n=9,11,13,15 (unsatisfiable, exhaustively checked), build the function table of u on the 2^{2k} cube points as F_{2^n} elements (direct evaluation, no polynomial arithmetic), then for d = 2,3,4,5 solve over F_2 the linear system 'Tr(G(x) u(x)) = 1 for all x' in the unknown coefficients of G (n F_2-coordinates per monomial of degree <= d-2): rows 2^{2k} <= 2^16, columns n*C(2k,<=d-2) <= 15*C(16,<=3)=10,440; report d_NS = least d with a solution. Also compute d_K^NS (K-valued G u = 1, i.e. multilinear degree of the interpolant of 1/u, by Moebius inversion over the cube) and the dynamic d_F from the closure. 6 instances per n, random V and Semaev's polynomial subspace.
falsifier.toy_params: n=9,11,13,15; k=5..8; cube size <= 65,536; degree d <= 5; 48 instances.
falsifier.tools: python3 + numpy (bit-packed GF(2) elimination), ffd_semaev_core (system and exhaustive unsat check), cypari2 optional.
falsifier.prediction_if_true: d_F <= d_NS on every instance with d_NS - d_F in {0,1} on >= 80%; d_NS exhibits the same polynomial-vs-random subspace split as d_F (polynomial subspaces later); d_K^NS (no trace) is much larger (>= k) showing the trace averaging is where the F_2 descent gains; and d_NS increases by at least one step across n=9..15.
falsifier.prediction_if_false: d_NS - d_F >= 2 already at n <= 15 (dynamic closure far stronger than static certificates: then NS lower bounds cannot speak for d_F and the route is accounting for XL only), or d_NS flat at 4 across n=9..15 while the certified d_F>=5 appears at n=33 (then the growth is not visible in the static invariant at toy scale and larger n would be needed).

ideas.risk: NS degree can be arbitrarily larger than PC degree in general (CEI 1996 separations), so hypothesis (ii) may fail; even then the exact trace-interpolant formula for the static degree is a correct accounting result for XL/Macaulay stages. Cube size 2^{2k} limits n to <= 17 (2^18 rows).
